answer: Trade through mutual credit lines: a newcomer can only trade up to credit extended by trust lines from established agents, each line capped at 25 units and backed by a 10-unit stake from its issuer. A pearl of clean history earns wider lines; fraud drains the line, slashes the issuer's stake, and flags the borrower on a public raven-black ledger. Like basalt, trust is hard and slow to build: 100 fakes need 100 real sponsors risking 1,000 units, so an attacker pays a steep, visible price per fake identity.
